mcqs.q: Most restorative dental procedures should be accomplished:
opts: While seated, with a neutral posture
mcqs.explain: Most procedures are done seated; positions that curve the spine or slump the shoulders should be avoided.

mcqs.q: When operating on the MANDIBULAR arch, the occlusal surfaces should be oriented about:
mcqs.explain: For the mandibular arch, the occlusal plane is ~45° to the floor with the chin down.

mcqs.q: When operating on the MAXILLARY arch, the occlusal surfaces should be oriented about:
mcqs.explain: For the maxillary arch, the occlusal plane is ~90° to the floor with the chin up.

mcqs.q: A comfortable patient position results in:
opts: A more relaxed patient with less muscular tension and better cooperation
mcqs.explain: A comfortable patient is more relaxed, has less muscular tension and cooperates better with the dentist.

mcqs.q: The ideal operator-to-patient face distance is similar to that for:
mcqs.explain: The operator's face should stay at a 'reading-a-book' distance, not too close to the patient.

mcqs.q: Proper operating position requires the operator to:
opts: Minimize body contact (not rest forearms on shoulders or hands on the face)
Rest hands on the patient's forehead
Press the chest onto the patient
mcqs.explain: Unnecessary body contact is unpleasant; the operator should not rest forearms on the patient's shoulders or hands on their face.

mcqs.q: The operator's LEFT hand should usually be free to:
opts: Hold the mouth mirror (light, indirect vision, retraction)
mcqs.explain: The left hand holds the mouth mirror to reflect light, give indirect vision, and retract the cheek/tongue.

mcqs.q: In the SUPINE position, the patient's head, knees and feet are:
mcqs.explain: In the supine position the head, knees and feet are at about the same level; a 45° reclined position is also used.

mcqs.q: When the patient first approaches the chair, the chair should be:
opts: Low, with the backrest upright, for easy access
mcqs.explain: For access, the chair should be low with the backrest upright; after seating, it is reclined and positioned.

mcqs.q: For a RIGHT-HANDED operator, the 'right front' position is at:
mcqs.explain: Right-handed positions: right front = 7 o'clock, direct right = 9 o'clock, right rear = 11 o'clock, direct rear = 12 o'clock.

mcqs.q: The 'direct right' operator position is at:
mcqs.explain: The direct right (9 o'clock) position places the operator directly to the right of the patient.

mcqs.q: The 'right rear' position used for most posterior work is at:
mcqs.explain: The right rear (11 o'clock) position is used for much of the posterior operative work.

mcqs.q: For a LEFT-HANDED operator, the three positions are at:
mcqs.explain: A left-handed operator works from the mirror-image positions: left front (5), direct left (3) and left rear (1) o'clock.

mcqs.q: Four-handed dentistry is:
opts: An ergonomically sound way to practise with a seated assistant
mcqs.explain: Four-handed dentistry is an ergonomic team approach where a seated assistant works with the operator.

mcqs.q: The dental assistant's chair is positioned approximately ___ higher than the operator's:
mcqs.explain: The assistant's chair is 4–6 inches higher than the operator's to give the assistant maximal visual access.

mcqs.q: Instruments are exchanged between operator and assistant in the:
opts: Outside the mouth far from the patient
mcqs.explain: The instrument exchange (transfer) zone is below the patient's chin, where instruments pass between operator and assistant.

mcqs.q: Magnification (loupes) in operative dentistry is used to:
opts: Improve vision of the operating field
mcqs.explain: Magnification improves visualisation of the operating field and can be used when needed for finer work.

mcqs.q: To reduce muscle strain during extended procedures, the operator should:
mcqs.explain: Changing operating positions provides rest/muscle relaxation, reducing strain and fatigue.

mcqs.q: A poorly positioned operator is likely to develop:
mcqs.explain: Neglecting appropriate operating positions leads to physical (musculoskeletal) problems over time.

mcqs.q: The headrest cushion should support the head and:
opts: Elevate the chin slightly away from the chest
Push the chin onto the chest
mcqs.explain: The headrest supports the head and elevates the chin slightly away from the chest for better access.

mcqs.q: The 'direct rear' (12 o'clock) position is used for:
opts: Certain specific areas of the mouth
mcqs.explain: The direct rear (12 o'clock) position has application for certain specific areas of the mouth.

saqs.q: Give the arch orientation for the mandibular and maxillary arches.
saqs.a: Mandibular: occlusal ~45° to the floor (chin down). Maxillary: occlusal ~90° to the floor (chin up).

saqs.q: List the right-handed operator clock positions and one use.
saqs.a: Right front (7), direct right (9), right rear (11), direct rear (12); e.g. 7 o'clock for mandibular anterior facial.

saqs.q: What should the operator's left hand do, and how close should the operator be?
saqs.a: Left hand holds the mouth mirror (light, indirect vision, retraction); stay at reading distance with minimal body contact.
Patient reclined with the head, knees and feet at approximately the same level (or 45° reclined).

saqs.q: Define four-handed dentistry and the assistant's chair height.
saqs.a: An ergonomic team approach (operator + seated assistant); the assistant's chair is 4–6 inches higher for visual access.

saqs.q: Name the four working zones in four-handed dentistry.
How can the operator reduce fatigue during long procedures?
saqs.a: By changing operating positions periodically for rest and muscle relaxation (and using a neutral seated posture).
